SeriesTraverseAccessor::find_neq¶

Back to SeriesTraverseAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseAccessor::find_neq(double rhs) const;
TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseAccessor::find_neq(const Series& rhs) const;

TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseProxy::find_neq(double rhs) const;
TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseProxy::find_neq(const Series& rhs) const;

What It Does¶

find_neq(rhs) is the negation of find_eq(rhs): it returns the coordinates of every position whose value is not equal to rhs. It is find_all with the mask source.ne(rhs).

Both the scalar and the peer-Series forms behave exactly as in find_eq, just inverted. See that page for the shape rule, broadcasting, gradient behavior, and the exact-equality caveat.

Parameters¶

rhs (double or const Series&)

The value that matched positions must differ from. A Series rhs is broadcast against the traversed shape.

Returns¶

TraverseMatch Coordinates and values of the non-equal positions, row-major.

Example¶

auto board = pluss::make_series({
    {1.0, 0.0, 1.0},
    {0.0, 1.0, 0.0},
});

auto not_one = board.traverse.find_neq(1.0);

std::cout << "count=" << not_one.count() << "\n";
std::cout << not_one.coords();

Output¶

count=3
pluss::Series(shape=[3,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[0, 1],
  [1, 0],
  [1, 2]]

Every position that is not 1 — the complement of find_eq(1.0) on the same board.
